question: Should OpenClaw adopt experiment-gated Claw lifecycle ownership diagnostics as a core doctor surface once the read-only sidecar defect and prerequisite stack are resolved?
rationale: The patch adds a new core lifecycle capability tied to an open RFC and compatibility-sensitive persisted ownership model; implementation quality cannot decide whether OpenClaw should permanently own and support that product contract.

options.title: Sponsor after contract repair
options.body: Accept the core diagnostics direction after the WAL-safe read path, real proof, prerequisite ownership contract, and RFC acceptance are complete.

options.title: Evaluate with the full stack
options.body: Keep this draft open but unlanded until maintainers review the complete Claws lifecycle series and its upgrade behavior together.

options.title: Decline the core direction
options.body: Close the implementation stack if Claw packaging, ownership, and lifecycle reconciliation should not become a core OpenClaw capability.

recommendation.title: Sponsor after contract repair
recommendation.body: Accept the core diagnostics direction after the WAL-safe read path, real proof, prerequisite ownership contract, and RFC acceptance are complete.

likelyOwner.reason: They supplied the product-model revision used by the current RFC and are the strongest visible owner for whether that model becomes a supported core contract.
